brief12.title: Choose Faith, Choose Love
notes: Slide text:
A Change of Choices (6)
By Faith or by Sight, Love or Hate
“We walk by faith, not by sight.”
(2 Corinthians 5:7)
Key points:
• Welcome everyone: this is Lesson 108 of Morning Devotion 321.
• Two main threads: by faith / by sight, love / hate.
• Stress that this is not a difference in behaviour but between two systems of life.
• Key verse: 2 Corinthians 5:7 — read the full verse first.

brief12.title: You Live in Your Choices
notes: Slide text:
You don’t live in your circumstances;
you live in your “choices.”
By faith, or by sight?
Choose love, or choose hate?
Key points:
• Ask: since this morning, how many choices have you made?
• Small choices pile up into character; character piles up into destiny.
• Deuteronomy 30:19: “Therefore choose life.”
• The self-centred system has self at the centre; the selfless system has God at the centre.

brief12.title: Key Verses and Background
notes: Slide text:
2 Cor 5:7: Paul writing in affliction
“We walk by faith, not by sight.”
1 John 3:18: John’s counsel in old age
“…but in deed and truth.”
Key points:
• Paul wrote 2 Corinthians around AD 55–57.
• 2 Corinthians 1:8: weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power.
• Words of faith grow out of the depths of suffering, not plucked from easy times.
• John in old age faced Gnosticism: saying they loved God while hating their brothers.

brief12.title: 1. By Faith
notes: Slide text:
Not failing to see,
but seeing “what God has said.”
The hen sees eggs,
but believes in chicks. (Heb 11:1)
Key points:
• Hebrews 11:1: “assurance”, hypostasis, a title deed.
• Faith is not a mood; it is a deed signed by God.
• The hen sits for twenty-one days, and all she sees is eggs.
• Generally credited to Martin Luther King Jr.: take the first step without seeing the whole staircase.

brief12.title: 2. By Sight
notes: Slide text:
Circumstances, resources, feelings
Result: anxiety, fear, retreat
Lot lifted up his eyes (Gen 13:10)
Abraham, by faith, became father of faith
Key points:
• The amygdala triggers fight-or-flight, suppressing the prefrontal cortex’s rational thought.
• 321: rely on the brain and ourselves and we worry; rely on the heart and the Holy Spirit and we rejoice.
• Genesis 13: Abram lays down his right to choose first — humility.
• Genesis 19:16: “But he lingered.”

brief12.title: 3. Crisis Reveals the System
notes: Slide text:
Invisible when all goes smoothly
Crisis, pressure, uncertainty
By sight: worry, fear, control
By faith: look to, wait on, lean on the Lord
Key points:
• Tea-bag illustration: boiling water doesn’t change what’s inside; it reveals it.
• Matthew 14:30–31: Peter saw the wind was strong and was afraid.
• What changed was not the wind but his eyes; the focus is Jesus, not circumstances.
• 2 Kings 6:17: ask the Lord to open our eyes, not to change our circumstances.

brief12.title: 4. Love Overflows from Selflessness
notes: Slide text:
Love is not a feeling; it is a choice
Giving, sacrificing, thinking of others
“Just as I have loved you,
you also love one another.” (John 13:34)
Key points:
• Agape is a decision of the will, which is why the Bible can command us to love.
• 1 Corinthians 13:4–5: doesn’t seek its own way.
• Baumeister, 2001, “Bad Is Stronger Than Good”: negative impact is stronger.
• Gottman: stable marriages keep positive to negative interactions at about five to one.

brief12.title: 5. Hate Is the Self-Centred Reaction
notes: Slide text:
Unwilling to let go, forgive, give way
“He did it to me first”
“Why on earth should I give way?”
“Turn to him the other also” (Matt 5:39)
Key points:
• Striking the right cheek meant a backhand: the point is not pain but humiliation.
• Turning the other cheek is not weakness; it is laying down our rights and living in God’s system.
• 321: pride provokes pride and both lose; humility draws out humility and both win.
• Witvliet’s 2001 study: grudges raise blood pressure and heart rate.

brief12.title: 6. The Source of Love; 7. Toward Perfection
notes: Slide text:
“We love him, because he first loved us.”
Not love because I have love — choose love
Perfect = ever more like the Father (Matt 5:48)
Key points:
• Protos: God’s love comes first; our love is a response.
• Tap illustration: the problem isn’t a lack of water, but not being connected.
• Corrie ten Boom: she reached out first, and then the warmth came.
• Teleios is not flawlessness, but reaching the purpose we were made for — maturity.

brief12.title: Putting It into Practice
notes: Slide text:
Choose faith in your circumstances
Deliberately choose a loving response
Reflect on God’s love every day
Eight stages: Information to Multiplication
Key points:
• Practice one: declare the promise first, then deal with the matter — the order must not be reversed.
• Practice two: pray once for the person who wronged you, and speak one sentence of blessing.
• Practice three: read “God so loved the world” as “God so loved me.”
• Eight stages: Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication.

brief12.title: Two Roads, Two Systems
notes: Slide text:
By sight → fear → self-centred
By faith → peace → selfless
Hate → bondage; love → victory
Choose faith, choose love
Key points:
• Joshua 24:15: choose today.
• Call one: put the egg you’ve sat on so long back in the nest and keep waiting.
• Call two: bring that name to mind; let them go today, and you will be free too.
• This is letting Jesus be King and letting Jesus receive all the glory.

brief12.title: Prayer of Response and Blessing
notes: Slide text:
Lord, I choose to live by faith
I choose love, no longer living in hate
Let your life be lived out in me
Live selfless; let Jesus be everything
Key points:
• Lead everyone in speaking this declaration of faith aloud together.
• Pray for those who can see no way forward: ask the Lord to open their eyes.
• Pray for those carrying bitterness: ask the Lord to give the power to forgive.
• Blessing: may the Lord’s love be poured out on you; may your choices today glorify his name.

brief21.title: Choose Faith, Choose Love
notes: Slide text:
A Change of Choices (6)
By Faith or by Sight, Love or Hate
“We walk by faith, not by sight.”
(2 Corinthians 5:7)
Key points:
• Morning Devotion 321, Lesson 108, thirty-minute version.
• Two main threads: faith and sight, love and hate.
• Two systems: the self-centred and the selfless.
• Read the full key verse first.

brief21.title: How Many Choices Have You Made?
notes: Slide text:
Since you opened your eyes this morning,
how many choices have you made?
Small choices pile up into character;
character piles up into destiny.
Key points:
• Open with everyday scenes: getting up, praying first or checking your phone first.
• Most choices are so small we don’t even notice them.
• Circumstances are only the stage; our choices are the script.
• Lead into: we don’t live in our circumstances; we live in our choices.

brief21.title: Two Systems
notes: Slide text:
Self-centred: self at the centre
Selfless: God at the centre
“Therefore choose life”
(Deuteronomy 30:19)
Key points:
• The self-centred looks at: my feelings, my rights, whether I’m losing out.
• The selfless looks at: what God has said, what God wants to do.
• Deuteronomy 30:19: God sets life and death, blessing and curse before us.
• God never forces us; he respects our choices, yet longs for us to choose rightly.

brief21.title: Key Verses and Background
notes: Slide text:
2 Cor 5:7: Paul writing in affliction
“Weighed down exceedingly” (2 Cor 1:8)
1 John 3:18: John’s counsel in old age
“…but in deed and truth.”
Key points:
• Paul wrote it around AD 55–57 in Macedonia.
• Corinth was a trading port where wealth and lust were plain to see.
• 2 Corinthians 4:18: the things seen are temporal; the things not seen are eternal.
• John faced Gnosticism: grand talk of knowledge, contempt for practice.

brief21.title: 1. Defining Faith
notes: Slide text:
Not failing to see,
but seeing “what God has said.”
“Faith is assurance of things hoped for,
proof of things not seen.” (Heb 11:1)
Key points:
• Dia pisteos: pistis means both faith and faithfulness.
• The weight of faith rests not in faith itself but in the one faith is placed in.
• Hypostasis: a foundation, a title deed; elegchos: conclusive evidence in court.
• Faith is not an optimistic mood; it is a deed signed by God.

brief21.title: Unseen Doesn’t Mean Absent
notes: Slide text:
Hubble exposed for ten days,
revealing over 3,000 galaxies
The hen sees eggs, believes in chicks
Twenty-one days of costly waiting
Key points:
• December 1995, the Hubble Deep Field: unseen only means not exposed long enough.
• The human eye sees only a tiny sliver of visible light in the electromagnetic spectrum.
• The hen sits twenty-one days, turning the eggs daily: not waiting for a miracle, but taking part in a process.
• Hebrews 11:27: as seeing him who is invisible.

brief21.title: 2. Three Ways of Living by Sight
notes: Slide text:
Circumstances, resources, feelings
Result: anxious, afraid, quick to retreat
The problem isn’t “looking”,
but making sight the final standard
Key points:
• Bandura, 1977, self-efficacy: what we believe shapes what we do.
• Christian faith rises far above self-efficacy: not believing in ourselves, but in God.
• The amygdala triggers fight-or-flight, suppressing the prefrontal cortex’s rational thought.
• 321: rely on the brain and ourselves and we worry; rely on the heart and the Holy Spirit and we rejoice.

brief21.title: Abraham and Lot
notes: Slide text:
The same starting point
Different choices
Utterly different endings
“But he lingered” (Gen 19:16)
Key points:
• Genesis 13: Abram lays down his right to choose first — humility.
• Lot “lifted up his eyes, and saw” the plain; God told Abram to lift up his eyes and look.
• Lifting his own eyes, Lot saw a plain; at God’s word, Abram saw “forever.”
• Genesis 3:6: Eve too “saw” first — humanity’s first failure was living by sight.

brief21.title: 3. Moments of Crisis
notes: Slide text:
When things go smoothly, you can’t tell
Crisis, pressure, uncertainty
reveal which system you live in
Boiling water shows what tea is in the bag
Key points:
• Three scenes: the doctor’s face, the layoff list, the child who won’t reply.
• Boiling water doesn’t change what’s in the tea bag; it reveals it.
• C. S. Lewis: pain is God’s megaphone to rouse a deaf world.
• A crisis is not God making things hard for you; it is God waking you up.

brief21.title: Two Responses
notes: Slide text:
By sight: worry, fear, control
By faith: look to, wait on, lean on the Lord
Faith is not the absence of feelings;
it’s trusting God above our feelings
Key points:
• Wanting control is pride: leaving our originally intended position, seizing rights, taking God’s place.
• Looking up, waiting, leaning are all movements of unclenching the hand — humility.
• Psalm 56:3: when I am afraid, I will put my trust in you.
• Mark 9:24: I believe. Help my unbelief!

brief21.title: 4. Love Is a Choice
notes: Slide text:
Love is not a feeling; it is a choice
Giving, sacrificing, thinking of others
“Just as I have loved you,
you also love one another.” (John 13:34)
Key points:
• Agape is a decision of the will, so it can be commanded.
• Eros, philia and storge rest on feelings; agape rests on choice.
• In all three the subject is me and the object is others — this is selflessness.
• 1 John 3:16: he laid down his life for us; by this we know love.

brief21.title: The Difficulty and Power of Love
notes: Slide text:
Hurt, yet still choosing love
Rejected, yet still choosing to accept
Wronged, yet still choosing to forgive
“Doesn’t seek its own way” (1 Cor 13:5)
Key points:
• Baumeister, 2001, “Bad Is Stronger Than Good”: negative impact is stronger.
• Gottman: stable marriages keep positive to negative interactions at about five to one.
• One hurt takes five acts of kindness to make up for, so love must rest on choice.
• The 920 practice: everyone is my “2”; practise living out the “0” and bearing the ninefold fruit.

brief21.title: 5. The Three Unwillings of Hate
notes: Slide text:
Unwilling to let go, forgive, give way
“Why on earth should I give way?”
“Turn to him the other also”
(Matthew 5:39)
Key points:
• None of the three is “can’t”; all are “won’t”. The self-centred life says, “I feel I’m in the right.”
• Striking a right cheek with the right hand meant a backhand: the point is not pain but humiliation.
• Turning the other cheek is not weakness; it is laying down our rights and living in God’s system.
• 321: pride provokes pride and both lose; humility draws out humility and both win.
