1. Question one: why don’t all the leaves fall? Answer: because there is life.
2. Science note: at the base of the leaf stalk there is an “abscission layer”; while the leaf is alive it produces auxin, the layer doesn’t form, and the leaf doesn’t fall.
3. Quote John 15:5, “He who remains in me … bears much fruit” — holding on is straining; remaining is rest.
4. Question two: why doesn’t a fish in salt water turn salty? Seawater is about 3.5 per cent salt; the fish actively pumps out salt through cells on its gills (osmoregulation).
5. Examples: Daniel in Babylon, Joseph in Egypt, Paul in prison in Rome — far saltier surroundings, yet they didn’t become salt fish.

The old, self-centred life: weak, quick to sin
The new life of Jesus: holy and victorious
The question isn’t which one exists
But which one you feed

2. The new self: Ephesians 4:24, “righteousness and holiness of truth”; Galatians 2:20, “it is no longer I who live, but Christ”.
3. Galatians 5:17: the flesh lusts against the Spirit — the fact that the war goes on shows the new life is still there.
4. Psychology: Daniel Wegner’s 1987 “white bear experiment” and the rebound effect.

Beat the black dog, and it grows fiercer
Feed the white dog, and it wins
The key isn’t defeating the black dog
The key is feeding the white dog

2. Beat the black dog and it grows fiercer; ignore it and put all your heart into feeding the white dog, and the white dog wins.
3. Charles Duhigg, The Power of Habit (2012): a habit is made up of cue, routine and reward; the golden rule is to replace, not delete.
4. Wendy Wood’s 2002 research: about 43 per cent of everyday behaviour is habit in fixed settings.
5. 321 application: pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility draws out humility, and both sides win. James 4:7 — first submit to God, then resist the devil.

“Put to death your members which are on the earth”
Colossians 3:5: treat it as a corpse
No opportunity, no room, no resources
Let it wither on its own

1. “Put to death” is the Greek nekroō, from the root nekros = a corpse; it means treating it as a corpse.
2. Colossians 3:3, “For you died”; Galatians 5:24, “have crucified the flesh” — a completed action.

4. The empty house (Matthew 12:44-45): swept clean but empty, and the spirit returns with seven worse than itself.

Victory isn’t my being stronger

Give today’s first bite to Christ
Let Jesus be King and receive all the glory

Because there is life, overcoming gravity
The leaf isn’t “clinging” to the tree
“Remains in me” John 15:5
Key points:
1. Ask: why don’t all the leaves fall? Answer: because there is life.
2. Science note: the “abscission layer” at the base of the leaf stalk; while the leaf is alive it produces auxin, and the layer doesn’t form.
3. Stress that the leaf isn’t “clinging” to the tree; it is joined to it and receiving supply.
4. Quote John 15:5: holding on is straining; remaining is rest.
2. The Parable of the Fish
Seawater salinity: about 3.5 per cent
A living fish pumps out salt every day
A living fish isn’t changed by its environment
A dead fish is salt fish in two days
Key points:
1. Ask: why doesn’t a fish in salt water become salt fish? Answer: because it is alive.
2. Data: seawater is about 3.5 per cent salt; a marine fish’s body fluids are only about a third as salty as seawater.
3. Mechanism: osmoregulation — constantly drinking, actively pumping out salt through cells on the gills, passing only a little concentrated urine.
4. Examples: Daniel in Babylon, Joseph in Egypt, Paul in prison in Rome.
5. 321 application: shift from man’s perspective to God’s — environment doesn’t decide life; life overcomes environment.
3. The Two Lives Within You
The old man grows corrupt after the lusts
The new man: righteousness and holiness of truth
Ephesians 4:22-24
Two lives contend within you
Key points:
1. Ephesians 4:22: the old self “grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit” — it needs no cultivating; it goes bad by itself.
2. Ephesians 4:24: the new self has “righteousness and holiness of truth”; Galatians 2:20, “it is no longer I who live”.
3. Galatians 5:17: the flesh lusts against the Spirit.
4. Comfort: the fact that the war goes on shows there is a new life within you that refuses to surrender.
3. The Question Is Which One You Feed
Don’t think of a white bear — and you think of it more
Wegner, 1987: the “rebound effect”
You think you’re combating it
In fact you’re feeding it
Key points:
1. The turning-point line: the question isn’t which one exists, but which one you feed.
2. Psychology: Daniel Wegner’s 1987 white bear experiment, published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
3. The result and the rebound effect: the more it is forbidden, the more people think of it, and once the ban is lifted it rebounds even higher.
4. Commonly attributed to Martin Luther: “You cannot stop the birds from flying over your head, but you can stop them from building a nest in your hair.”
5. In 321 language: the old self is self-centred, the new self is selfless; selflessness is not having nothing, but entering into the infinite.
4. The Black Dog and the White Dog
A farmer keeps a black dog and a white dog
Beat the black dog, and it grows fiercer
Ignore the black dog, feed the white dog
In the end the white dog wins
Key points:
1. Tell the story of the black dog and the white dog (generally thought to come from a Native North American legend; its true origin can’t be traced).
2. The first part: the black dog keeps eating and grows fiercer; beat it and it grows fiercer still, lock it up and it barks all night.
3. The turn: the farmer ignores the black dog and puts all his heart into feeding the white dog.
4. The ending: the white dog simply stands there, and the black dog backs away.
4. Not Defeating, but Feeding
Duhigg: habits can’t be deleted
Only the routine in the middle can be replaced
“Be subject to God. Resist the devil” James 4:7
Submit first, then resist
Key points:
1. Key line: the key isn’t defeating the black dog; it is feeding the white dog.
2. Charles Duhigg, The Power of Habit (2012): cue, routine, reward; the golden rule is to replace, not delete.
3. Wendy Wood’s 2002 research: about 43 per cent of everyday behaviour is habit in fixed settings.
4. James 4:6-7: God gives grace to the humble; first submit to God, then resist the devil.
5. 321 application: pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility draws out humility, and both sides win.
5. The True Meaning of “Put to Death”
“Put to death your members which are on the earth”
Colossians 3:5
Put to death = treat it as a corpse
No opportunity, no room, no resources
Key points:
1. Read the full verse, Colossians 3:5, including “covetousness, which is idolatry”.
2. Greek: nekroō, from the root nekros = a corpse; it means treating it as a corpse.
3. Colossians 3:3, “For you died”; Galatians 5:24, “have crucified the flesh” — a completed action.
4. The weeds illustration: cutting the weeds is combating; cutting off the water is putting to death.
5. Emptying Must Be Followed by Filling
The house swept and empty: seven worse spirits return
Matthew 12:44-45
“But be filled with the Spirit” Ephesians 5:18
Combating isn’t enough — we must cultivate
Key points:
1. The empty house (Matthew 12:44-45): empty, swept and put in order — yet empty.
2. Name the problem: the combating was a great success, but no new master moved in.
3. Ephesians 5:18: “Don’t be drunken with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit.”
4. Romans 8:13: “If by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.” Stress “by the Spirit”.
5. 321 application: the Holy Spirit is my guide — even putting to death is not my own construction project.
6. Every Day You Are Feeding
Humility, faith, love: feeding selflessness
Pride, fear, hatred: feeding the self-centred life
“Whatever a man sows, that he will also
reap” Galatians 6:7
Key points:
1. Every choice feeds something — humility or pride, faith or fear, love or hatred; there is no neutral ground.
2. Galatians 6:7-8: “Don’t be deceived … whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.”
3. Neuroscience: Donald Hebb, The Organization of Behavior (1949) — repeated firing strengthens connections.
4. Illustration: every time you lose your temper, you tread that path in your brain wider and easier to walk.
5. Proverbs 4:23: “out of it is the wellspring of life.”
7. The Real Road to Victory
Victory isn’t my trying harder
It is the life of Jesus growing stronger
“Our inward man is renewed day by day”
2 Corinthians 4:16
Key points:
1. Victory isn’t my trying harder or my being stronger; it is the life of Jesus growing stronger.
2. 2 Corinthians 4:16: “Our inward man is renewed day by day” — cultivating is a small supply each day.
3. Three effects: the pull of sin declines, the struggle lessens, victory happens naturally.
4. Augustine, Confessions: “You have made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.”
5. Concluding line: not combating sin, but living out life (John 10:10, “have it abundantly”).
Putting It into Practice (1) (2)
Recognise what you are feeding
Three minutes at bedtime: a two-column reflection
Deliberately feed the life of Jesus
Prayer, Bible reading, obeying the Holy Spirit
Key points:
1. Practice one: a three-minute two-column reflection at bedtime — left column feeding selflessness, right column feeding the self-centred life; just write, no condemnation.
2. Evaluation and Repetition: after a week, see which column is longer; do it for thirty days. Multiplication: teach a brother or sister to do it with you.
3. Practice two: 1 Peter 2:2, “long for the pure milk of the Word”; set a portion so small you’ll certainly manage it.
4. Psalm 1:3, “like a tree planted by the streams of water” — a tree doesn’t grow up in a day; it puts down roots day after day.
Putting It into Practice (3) and the Eight Stages
Stop feeding self-centred habits
Less complaining, comparing, judging
Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation
Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication
Key points:
1. Practice three: Romans 13:14, “make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts”.
2. Ask the Holy Spirit to point out which time of day, which chat group, which app is preparing the black dog’s dinner.
3. Implementation: remove one this week and add one thing that feeds selflessness; emptying must always be followed by filling.
4. Name the eight stages one by one: Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication.
5. Philippians 4:8: whatever you think about, you feed.
The 3-2-1 Vision in Summary
Jesus my role model, the Bible my standard, the Spirit my guide
Let Jesus be King and receive all the glory
Change your mindset and your life changes
The 920 practice, 235 relationships
Key points:
1. The Three Foundations: Jesus is my role model (Philippians 2:7, “emptied himself”), the Bible is my standard (the original meaning of “put to death”), the Holy Spirit is my guide (Romans 8:2, 13).
2. The Two Core Values: whomever you feed, you let reign as king; if victory came from my straining, the glory would be stolen.
3. The Goal: establish God’s system, passing the principle of life on to the next person.
4. The fivefold change: mindset, life, daily living, relationships, ministry; life first, then relationships, then ministry.
5. The 920 practice and 235 relationships: everyone I relate to is my “2”; find a companion to feed the white dog with you, so you don’t grow slack.
Closing and Call
No need to defeat the darkness — turn on the light
Feed self, lose more; feed selflessness, win more
Give today’s first bite to Christ
Let Jesus be King and receive all the glory
Key points:
1. The lesson’s gentle reminder: you don’t have to defeat the darkness; you only need to turn on the light.
2. Darkness has no substance — you can’t hit it or push it; strike one match, and the darkness retreats.
3. Restate the conclusion: feed the self-centred life and you lose more and more; feed selflessness and you win more and more.
4. Call: give today’s first bite to Christ — your first thought, your first word, your first choice.
5. Point to the Two Core Values: let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory.
Response Prayer and Blessing
Lord, I choose to feed your life within me
And no longer feed the self-centred life
Let Christ grow within me
Living out a victorious, free and glorious life
Key points:
1. Lead the congregation in praying together, slowly and gently.
2. Confess the failure of combating in our own strength, and ask the Holy Spirit to show us whom we fed today.
3. Make the lesson’s declaration of faith: I choose to feed your life within me.
4. Close with a blessing, and encourage everyone to practise the “two-column reflection” this week.

script12.title: Not Combating, but Cultivating
script: Brothers and sisters, good morning. Today we come together to lesson 113 of Morning Devotion 321, entitled “Not Combating, but Cultivating”. This is the third lesson in our series on “A Change of Habits”. Our theme verse is Romans 8:2: “For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.” There is just one sentence I want to leave in your heart today: whichever you feed is the one that wins.

script12.title: Introduction: Two Men Quit Smoking
script: Brothers and sisters, let me begin with the story of two brothers who quit smoking. The first used “combating”. He threw out his cigarettes, smashed his lighter and put up a sign on the wall: “NO SMOKING!” And the result? All day long his mind was full of cigarettes, and on day eleven he bought a packet. The second was different. He went running, he learned the harmonica, he joined a prayer group. Three months later someone asked him how quitting was going, and he paused and said, “Oh — I don’t think I’ve thought about that for a long time.” Brothers and sisters, one gave it everything he had, and failed; the other went about it quietly, and overcame. Why? Because the harder we try, the weaker we get; the more we combat, the more we fail. God’s way is not combating; it is cultivating life.

script12.title: Theme Verse and Background
script: Let’s look first at the background. In Romans 7 there is a man struggling within himself. He says, “For the good which I desire, I don’t do; but the evil which I don’t desire, that I practice.” And in the end he cries out, “What a wretched man I am!” Brothers and sisters, have you noticed who the main character of chapter 7 is? It is “I”. The whole chapter is about me, and the whole chapter is failure. But as chapter 8 begins, the main character changes — to the Holy Spirit. Elsewhere, in Colossians 2:23, Paul says that those rules of severity to the body “aren’t of any value against the indulgence of the flesh”. God himself says: combating with all your strength has no value.

script12.title: 1. The Key to Overcoming Sin: the Law of Life
script: So the first point: the key to overcoming sin is the law of life. Romans 8:2 says there are two laws. One is the law of sin and of death; it is like gravity — you don’t have to do anything, and it pulls you down. The other is the law of the Spirit of life, which God has placed within you. Brothers and sisters, this verse doesn’t say, “Because I tried harder”; it says that law “made me free”. Put a piece of iron on a table, and gravity holds it down; bring a magnet above it, and the iron rises. Has gravity disappeared? No. It’s just that a stronger force has come in.

script12.title: 2. The Parable of the Leaf and the Fish
script: The second point is two parables. Let me ask you, brothers and sisters: why don’t all the leaves fall off the trees? If there were only gravity, every leaf ought to be on the ground. The answer is: because there is life. The leaf isn’t straining; the leaf is simply alive, simply joined to the tree. The Lord Jesus said, “He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit.” Another question: why doesn’t a fish soaking in salt water become salt fish? Because it is alive. A living fish pumps out salt every day. A dead fish is salt fish in two days. Brothers and sisters, the key isn’t the environment; the key is life.

script12.title: 3. The Two Lives Within You
script: The third point: there are two lives within you. One is the old, self-centred life, which sins easily, is easily lured, and is easily weak. Ephesians says the old self “grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit”. The other is the new life of Jesus: holy, victorious, free. These two lives are in competition within you. But brothers and sisters, the question isn’t which one exists — both exist. The question is which one you feed. In 1987 the psychologist Daniel Wegner carried out the white bear experiment: the more people were told not to think of a white bear, the more they thought of it. You think you’re combating it; in fact you’re feeding it.

script12.title: 4. The Black Dog and the White Dog
script: The fourth point is the black dog and the white dog. A farmer kept two dogs: the black dog stands for the self-centred life, the white dog for selflessness. At first the black dog kept eating and grew fiercer and fiercer, while the white dog grew weaker. The farmer beat the black dog, and it grew fiercer still. Later the farmer changed his strategy: he ignored the black dog and put all his heart into feeding the white dog. And the result? The white dog grew stronger and stronger, the black dog grew thinner and thinner, and in the end the white dog won. Brothers and sisters, the key isn’t “defeating the black dog”; the key is “feeding the white dog”. James says: first submit to God, then resist the devil. The order can’t be reversed.

script12.title: 5. What the Bible Means by “Put to Death”
script: The fifth point: what does the Bible really mean by “put to death”? Colossians 3:5 says, “Put to death therefore your members which are on the earth.” Many people take this to mean that we must combat sin with all our might. But the root of the Greek word for “put to death” means “a corpse”: it means treating it as a corpse. Galatians 5:24 says that those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh. So putting to death isn’t killing something that is alive; it is no longer feeding something that has already been ended. Give it no opportunity, no room, no resources, and let it wither on its own. The Lord Jesus told the parable of the empty house: the house was swept clean but empty, and the spirit came back with seven worse than itself. That is why Paul says, “Don’t be drunken with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit.” Emptying isn’t enough; there must also be filling.

script12.title: 6–7. Every Day You Are Feeding
script: Let me take the sixth and seventh points together. Brothers and sisters, every day you are feeding one life or the other. Choose humility, faith and love, and you feed selflessness; choose pride, fear and hatred, and you feed the self-centred life. You are feeding every day; you just haven’t noticed. Paul says, “Whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.” So what is the real road to victory? Not my trying harder, not my being stronger, but the life of Jesus growing stronger in me. When you give yourself to cultivating the life of Christ, the pull of sin naturally declines, the struggle naturally lessens, and victory naturally happens.

script12.title: Putting It into Practice
script: So what do we do? The lesson gives us three practices. First, recognise what you are feeding. Tonight before you sleep, spend three minutes: on the left write the choices you made today that fed selflessness, and on the right the choices that fed the self-centred life. Just write — no condemnation. Second, deliberately feed the life of Jesus. Prayer, Bible reading, obeying the Holy Spirit — set a portion so small you’ll certainly manage it. Third, stop feeding self-centred habits. A little less complaining, a little less comparing, a little less judging. But please remember: emptying must always be followed by filling.

script12.title: Closing and Call
script: Brothers and sisters, let me close with the lesson’s gentle reminder: you don’t have to defeat the darkness; you only need to turn on the light. If you fight the darkness, you can’t land a blow; but strike just one match, and the darkness retreats. Feed the self-centred life, and you lose more and more; feed selflessness, and you win more and more. This morning I’m not asking you to make a bigger vow; I’m asking you to do just one thing: give your first bite of today to Christ. Let Jesus reign as King in your heart; let Jesus receive all the glory.

script12.title: Response Prayer and Blessing
script: Let us pray together. Dear Lord Jesus, we thank you. We confess that for far too many years we have spent our strength combating ourselves, and the more we combated, the weaker we became. Today you have shown us that victory is not my being stronger; it is your life growing stronger in me. Lord, I choose to feed your life within me and no longer feed the self-centred life. Let Christ grow within me, so that I live out a victorious, free and glorious life. In the holy name of the Lord Jesus Christ we pray. Amen. May the Lord bless you, all through this day.

script21.title: Not Combating, but Cultivating
script: Brothers and sisters, good morning. Today we come together to lesson 113 of Morning Devotion 321, entitled “Not Combating, but Cultivating”. This is the third lesson in our series on “A Change of Habits”. Our theme verse is Romans 8:2: “For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.” Brothers and sisters, there is just one sentence I want to leave in your heart today: whichever you feed is the one that wins. May the Holy Spirit himself speak to us this morning.

script21.title: Introduction (1): Two Men Quit Smoking
script: Let me begin with the story of two brothers who quit smoking. The first brother’s method was “combating”. He threw out every cigarette in the house, smashed his lighter and put up a big poster on the wall: “NO SMOKING!” The first thing he did every morning when he got up was to tell himself, “Today I absolutely must not smoke.” And the result? He thought about cigarettes in meetings, he thought about them in traffic jams, and lying in bed he was still thinking about them. On day eleven he stood outside a convenience store for three minutes, then bought a packet. He went home, slumped on the sofa and said, “Just as I thought — I can’t do it.”

script21.title: Introduction (2): Combat More, Fail More
script: The second brother was different. He didn’t put the focus on “not smoking”. He signed up for the neighbourhood morning running group and every day ran three kilometres with a crowd of people; he started learning the harmonica, and whenever his hands were free he picked it up; he joined the church prayer group and every evening prayed for twenty minutes with two other brothers. Three months later someone asked him, “How’s quitting smoking going?” He paused for a moment and said, “Oh — I don’t think I’ve thought about that for a long time.” Brothers and sisters, one poured all his strength into combating, and failed; the other quietly set about cultivating, and overcame. So many people want to overcome sin, but they use the wrong method: combating with all their strength, suppressing with all their might, struggling without end. The harder they try, the weaker they get; the more they combat, the more they fail. God’s way is not combating; it is cultivating life.

script21.title: Theme Verse and Background
script: Let’s look first at the background. Paul wrote Romans in Corinth around AD 56 to 57, to the church in Rome, which he had never visited. To understand chapter 8, you must first read chapter 7. The man in chapter 7 says, “For the good which I desire, I don’t do; but the evil which I don’t desire, that I practice.” And in the end he cries out, “What a wretched man I am!” Brothers and sisters, notice that the word that appears most in chapter 7 is “I”. The main character of the whole chapter is me, and the whole chapter ends in failure. Colossians, for its part, Paul wrote from prison in Rome, at a time when the church was troubled by an ascetic heresy. What was Paul’s verdict? Colossians 2:23: “but aren’t of any value against the indulgence of the flesh.” God himself says: severity to the body has no value.

script21.title: 1. The Law of Life (Scripture)
script: So the first point: the key to overcoming sin is the law of life. Romans 8:2 says, “For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.” The word “law” in Greek is nomos: not only written rules, but “an ongoing operating principle”. It doesn’t need your agreement; it simply operates. And the word “made free” means buying a slave out of his master’s hand and taking off his chains. Brothers and sisters, listen carefully: this verse doesn’t say, “Because I tried harder”; it says that law “made me free”. The subject isn’t me.

script21.title: 1. The Law of Life (Illustration)
script: Let me give an illustration. Put a piece of iron on a table: gravity holds it down firmly, and you have to make an effort to lift it. But what happens if you hold a powerful magnet above it? The iron rises by itself. Tell me, has gravity disappeared? No — it hasn’t stopped working for one second. It’s just that a stronger force has come in and overcome it. Brothers and sisters, since you believed in the Lord, has the pull of sin disappeared? No. But God has placed a magnet within you — the Holy Spirit, the life of Christ. The key has never been that you try harder; the key is which law is operating within you.

script21.title: 2. The Parable of the Leaf
script: The second point is two parables. Let me ask you, brothers and sisters: why don’t all the leaves fall off the trees? If gravity were the only thing operating in the world, every leaf ought to be on the ground. The answer is: because there is life. And this can be verified. Where the leaf joins the twig there is a layer called the “abscission layer”; while the leaf is alive it keeps producing auxin, so the abscission layer doesn’t form, and the leaf stays firmly attached to the tree. Brothers and sisters, the leaf isn’t “clinging” to the tree; the leaf isn’t struggling; the leaf is simply alive. The Lord Jesus said, “He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit.” Holding on is straining; remaining is rest.

script21.title: 2. The Parable of the Fish
script: Now a second question: why doesn’t a fish soaking in salt water become salt fish? Seawater is about three and a half per cent salt. The answer is: because it is alive. In biology this is called “osmoregulation”. A marine fish’s body fluids are only about a third as salty as seawater, so it has to keep drinking and then use special cells on its gills to actively pump the excess salt out. It is an activity of life going on every second. A living fish pumps out salt every day, so it isn’t salty; put a dead fish in brine, and in two days it’s salt fish. Brothers and sisters, a living fish isn’t changed by its environment; only a dead fish is shaped by its surroundings. We often blame our environment, but Daniel in Babylon, Joseph in Egypt, Paul in prison in Rome — their environments were far saltier than ours. The key isn’t the environment; the key is life.

script21.title: 3. The Two Lives Within You
script: The third point: there are two lives within you. The first is the old, self-centred life, which sins easily, is easily lured, and is easily weak. Ephesians 4:22 says the old self “grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit”. Notice the words “grows corrupt” — the old self doesn’t need you to cultivate it; it goes bad all by itself. The second is the new life of Jesus: holy, victorious, free. Verse 24 says the new self, “in the likeness of God has been created in righteousness and holiness of truth”. Paul says, “For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh.” So, brothers and sisters, the fact that the war is still going on inside you shows precisely that there is a new life within you that refuses to surrender.

script21.title: 3. The Question Is Which One You Feed
script: But here comes a crucial turn. The question isn’t which life exists — both exist. The question is which one you feed. Psychology gives us powerful corroboration. In 1987 the American psychologist Daniel Wegner and his colleagues published the famous “white bear experiment”. He gave his participants just one instruction: “For the next five minutes, please don’t think of a white bear.” The result? Those told not to think of a white bear had one pop into their minds far more often than those given no such instruction. Wegner called this the “rebound effect”. Brothers and sisters, that is why combating with all your strength is doomed to fail. When you spend all day saying “I mustn’t”, you are in effect keeping that thing at the very centre of your thoughts all day long. You think you’re combating it; in fact you’re feeding it.

script21.title: 4. The Black Dog and the White Dog
script: The fourth point is the story of the black dog and the white dog. It is very widely told and is generally thought to come from a Native North American legend. A farmer kept two dogs: the black dog stands for the self-centred life, the white dog for selflessness. At first the black dog kept eating and grew fiercer and fiercer, while the white dog ate very little and grew thinner and weaker. Every time they fought, the black dog won. The farmer beat the black dog with a stick, and it grew fiercer still; he locked it up, and it barked all night. Later the farmer changed his strategy: he ignored the black dog — didn’t beat it, didn’t scold it, didn’t feed it — and put all his heart and energy into feeding the white dog. And the result? The white dog grew stronger and stronger, and the black dog grew thinner and weaker. One day the two dogs faced off again; the white dog simply stood there, and the black dog backed away. In the end, the white dog won.

script21.title: 4. Not Defeating, but Feeding
script: Brothers and sisters, remember the point: the key isn’t “defeating the black dog”; the key is “feeding the white dog”. Modern habit science confirms this principle too. In 2012 Charles Duhigg, in his book The Power of Habit, gathered up the academic research and pointed out that a habit is made up of three parts — cue, routine and reward — and that the golden rule of habit change is this: you can almost never pull an old habit out by the roots; what you can do is keep the same cue and reward and swap out the routine in the middle. Not deleting, but replacing. James 4:7 says, “Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” See the order: first submit to God, then resist the devil. First feed the white dog, and then the black dog runs away.

script21.title: 5. The True Meaning of “Put to Death”
script: The fifth point: what does the Bible really mean by “put to death”? Colossians 3:5 says, “Put to death therefore your members which are on the earth.” Many people take this to mean we must combat sin with all our might, and so they treat themselves harshly and live in self-reproach. But the Greek for “put to death” is nekroō, and its root nekros means “a corpse”. It doesn’t mean “to kill something that is alive”; it means “to treat it as a corpse”. Just before this, Paul has said, “For you died.” And Galatians 5:24 says that those who belong to Christ “have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts”. So the true meaning of putting to death is: don’t feed it. Give it no opportunity, no room, no resources, and let it wither on its own.

script21.title: 5. Emptying Must Be Followed by Filling
script: The Lord Jesus told a more sobering parable. An unclean spirit leaves a person, finds no rest in waterless places, and decides to return to the house it came from. “When he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order. Then he goes, and takes with himself seven other spirits more evil than he is.” Brothers and sisters, the combating in that house was a great success — the spirit had been driven out, the floor had been mopped clean, it had even been put in order. So where was the problem? The problem was that it was empty, with no new master. That is why Paul says, “Don’t be drunken with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit.” Emptying isn’t enough; there must also be filling. Combating isn’t enough; there must also be cultivating. Romans 8:13 says too, “If by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.” Look at those words: by the Spirit.

script21.title: 6. Every Day You Are Feeding
script: The sixth point: every day you are feeding one life or the other. Every one of your choices feeds either selflessness or the self-centred life; there is no neutral ground. Choose humility, and you feed selflessness; choose pride, and you feed the self-centred life. Choose faith, and you feed selflessness; choose fear, and you feed the self-centred life. Choose love, and you feed selflessness; choose hatred, and you feed the self-centred life. You are feeding every day; you just haven’t noticed. Paul says, “Don’t be deceived. God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.” Brothers and sisters, self-deception is thinking that one bite doesn’t count. But every bite counts. Neuroscience tells us that in 1949 Donald Hebb proposed that nerve cells which repeatedly fire together become ever more strongly connected. Every time you lose your temper, you tread that path in your brain a little wider.

script21.title: 7. The Real Road to Victory
script: The seventh point: the real road to victory. Victory isn’t “I try harder”; victory isn’t “I get stronger”; victory is “the life of Jesus grows stronger in me”. 2 Corinthians 4:16 says, “Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.” Renewed day by day — that is cultivating. When you give yourself to cultivating the life of Christ, three things happen: the pull of sin naturally declines — not because sin has grown ugly, but because Christ has grown beautiful; the struggle naturally lessens; and victory naturally happens. Augustine said, “You have made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.” Only God can fill the emptiness of the human heart. So it is not combating sin, but living out life.

script21.title: Putting It into Practice (1) (2)
script: So what do we do? The lesson gives us three practices. First, recognise what you are feeding. Tonight before you sleep, spend three minutes on a “two-column reflection”: in the left column write three choices you made today that fed selflessness, and in the right column three choices that fed the self-centred life. Just write — no condemnation. After a week, see which column is longer. Second, deliberately feed the life of Jesus. Through prayer, Bible reading and obeying the Holy Spirit, set a portion so small you’ll certainly manage it — three verses of the Bible, five minutes of prayer, one memory verse a day. 1 Peter says, “As newborn babies, long for the pure milk of the Word.” A tree doesn’t grow up in a day; a tree puts down roots day after day.

script21.title: Putting It into Practice (3) and the Eight Stages
script: Third, stop feeding self-centred habits. A little less complaining, a little less comparing, a little less judging. Romans 13:14 says, “But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts.” Brothers and sisters, ask the Holy Spirit to point out which “provision” in your daily living is really preparing the black dog’s dinner. Is it that time of day? That chat group? This week, pick one and remove it, and then add one thing that feeds selflessness. 321’s eight stages of changing our mindset are: Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication. Don’t stop at Information; go all the way to Multiplication — once you’ve tasted freedom, go and help those who are still struggling.

script21.title: The 3-2-1 Vision in Summary
script: Let’s set today’s truth within 321. The Three Foundations: Jesus is my role model — he “emptied himself, taking the form of a servant”, and emptying himself is the supreme role model of selflessness; the Bible is my standard — only by putting “put to death” back into the original did we see that it means to stop supplying; the Holy Spirit is my guide — from beginning to end, the power comes from the Holy Spirit. The Two Core Values: let Jesus be King — whomever you feed, you let reign as king; let Jesus receive all the glory — if victory came from my straining, I would be sure to feel a secret pride. The Goal: establish God’s system. Brothers and sisters, the fivefold change is mindset, life, daily living, relationships, ministry, and what we need to change today is the very first link: from “I must combat sin” to “I will cultivate life”. In the 920 practice, everyone you relate to is your “2”; in 235 relationships, find a companion to feed the white dog with you, and you won’t easily grow slack.

script21.title: Closing and Call
script: Brothers and sisters, let me close with the lesson’s gentle reminder: you don’t have to defeat the darkness; you only need to turn on the light. Have you ever tried fighting the darkness? No one can do it. Darkness has no substance; you can’t hit it and you can’t push it. But strike just one match, and the darkness retreats. There is a war going on inside you, but the key to who wins is simple: whom you feed. Feed the self-centred life, and you lose more and more; feed selflessness, and you win more and more. This morning I’m not asking you to make a bigger vow or to grit your teeth harder. I’m asking you to do something simpler and deeper — give your first bite of today to Christ. Hand your first thought to him, offer your first word to him, yield your first choice to him. Let Jesus reign as King in your heart; let Jesus receive all the glory.

script21.title: Response Prayer and Blessing
script: Let us pray together. Dear Lord Jesus, we thank you. We confess that for far too many years we have spent our strength combating ourselves, and the more we combated, the weaker we became. Today you have shown us that victory is not my being stronger; it is your life growing stronger in me. Lord, forgive us our past self-deception; shine your light on us, and let us see whom we have fed today. May the law of the Spirit of life work mightily within us, and set us free from the law of sin and of death. Let our black dog wither because its supply has been cut off, and let our white dog grow strong because it is fed every day. Lord, I choose to feed your life within me and no longer feed the self-centred life. Let Christ grow within me, so that I live out a victorious, free and glorious life. Reign as King in our hearts; may all the glory be yours. In the holy name of the Lord Jesus Christ we pray. Amen. May the Lord bless you and keep you, all through this day.
